scope: Scoped agent review of nine complete current native viewports for retained river continuity, headwater legibility, representative regional materials and UI framing. Not a commercial art approval.
observations: The inspected Hankou and Nanjing source-linked main channels retain a continuous visible water ribbon, including the mobile-layout Hankou frame.
The inspected Yanshan headwaters render as continuous thin lines rather than the earlier stippled subpixel-triangle artifact.
Dune sand, temperate litter and the first atlas page retain distinct source materials and the atlas exposes independent texture choices.
The inspected mountain, coast and river frames retain the complete normal HUD and native screenshot bytes; no unsupported river bends or islands were painted in.
remaining_visual_issues: Source-supported river and coastline geometry remains visibly angular at tactical zoom; primary ribbons still need more natural shore treatment within source constraints.
Local tactical administrative/control border strokes do not always visually coincide with the physical coastline; this release clips the Asian strategic control meshes, not all local boundary layers.
Continental ownership/terrain overlays still show large polygon and triangle patches; city and unit crowding reduces readability.
Full regional transition kits, location-specific ports and bridges, all-unit animation cycles and physical Motorola X30 verification remain outstanding.
